newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares rally on Shenzhen.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares rally on Shenzhen.

text.p: Shanghai B shares rallied for the sixth day in a row on Tuesday, encouraged by rises on the Shenzhen B shares market, brokers said.
The index rose 0.294 points or 0.63 percent to 47.104 points, on volume of 11.1 million shares worth $2.4 million. Of 41 B shares, 38 traded, with 21 up, 11 flat and six down.
Shenzhen B index surge 6.52 percent or 6.30 points to 102.86 with turnover of HK$81.2 million from Monday's HK$58.35 million.

Brokers said buying interest increased on the back of gains in Shenzhen B shares, which were stimulated by rumours that the authorities were planning to take measures to boost the bearish B share market.
"The recent string of rises has improved market sentiment to some extent, but the rate of the rise is slow with major institutions focusing their buying on Shenzhen," a broker said.

"The index has re-established itself above the key 47-point level, which encouraged investors very much," another broker said. "If overseas investors come in to buy in the coming days, we could see it hitting at least 50 points."

Shanghai Posts & Communication Equipment was the star on steady institutional position building around $0.280 on expectation of the company reaching its 1996 targets, brokers said. It rose $0.014 or 5.14 percent to $0.286 on volume of 410,900 shares.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere traded the most on inter-institutional trading, ending unchanged at $0.380 on volume of 663,200 shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development traded the second most, ending unchanged at $0.818 on volume of 640,300 shares.

Shanghai A share index rose with capital flowing in from the Shenzhen market, but ended off its intra-day high of 1104.614 points with some local institutions liquidating heavy positions late in the session, brokers said.

The A index was up 11.987 points or 1.13 percent to 1070.816 points, on volume of 1.2 billion shares worth 10.0 billion yuan. The SSE 30 Blue-Chip index fell 21.703 points or 0.82 percent to 2611.360 points.
Yaohua Glass was the star on institutional speculative buying, surging 1.91 yuan or 20.96 percent to 11.02 yuan on volume of 7.5 million shares.
